messages:
Alex P.: Heads up — after the kernel-selection push last night we saw a cluster-wide p95 latency bump (~20%) on Mixtral MoE endpoints. Correlated with router-score volatility and a KV cache eviction spike. anyone on call? :thinking:
Mica Chen: I pulled router logits for a 1h window. distribution widened a lot — stdev jumped from ~1.1 -> ~2.9. top-k selection is noisier, so routing fanout effectively increased. brief snippet from the dump:
```
router_logits.mean=1.18
router_logits.std=2.92
previous.std=1.09
topk_config=2
softmax_temp=1.0 (unchanged in model cfg but runtime path may be different)
```
Samir: Suspect numerical drift from the new int8-accelerated kernel path. small FP diffs in matmul/linear can change softmax ranking for borderline logits — that cascades in MoE. Did the kernel selector flip to a different GEMM impl for specific shapes?
Lina G.: I also saw KV cache metrics: cache_miss_rate p50 went 4% -> 17%, eviction rate spiked, and per-expert queue length increased on the same subset of requests. looks like hot-expert thrash.
Alex P.: Good catch. That explains latency — more misses => recompute KV => longer loops. Can we add a quick guard: force deterministic topk or pin to fallback GEMM for Mixtral MoE in canary?
Mica Chen: I ran a quick local experiment forcing the old kernel; router_logits stdev reverted to ~1.2 and cache miss rate dropped in the trace. So yes, kernel path change is correlated.
Samir: Here’s the problematic snippet from the kernel selector logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-06-23T03:12:18Z] kernel_selector: selected_xy_gemm_v2(shape=4096x3072) path=int8_fast fallback=f32_ref
[2026-06-23T03:12:18Z] kernel_selector: quantize_bias=true reorder_kv=true
```
Small reorder/packing differences + quantization bias can shift logits. For MoE topk that is enough.
Lina G.: Two immediate levers I propose:
1) increase per-expert cache capacity for Mixtral canary (reduce evictions)
2) experiment with moe-expert-parallelism to spread load (4->8) and measure queue lengths
3) force deterministic/topk-stable selection on router if available
Alex P.: Agreed. Also want to test lowering router softmax temperature to reduce entropy so borderline logits don't flip as often. Mica, can you prepare a 5% canary with these three changes? include metric checks for route_skew, kv_miss_rate, per_expert_queue_ms, p95 latency.
Mica Chen: Will do. Proposed runtime overrides:
```
--moe-expert-cache-size=24GB
--moe-expert-parallelism=8
--router-topk=2 --router-temp=0.8
--moe-stable-topk=true  # runtime flag to use deterministic topk path
```
Samir: Note: stable-topk may be slower for very large batch kernels — expect a small comp overhead. but should be fine at 5% traffic.
perf-bot: Auto-post — flamegraph snapshot for the 03:10-03:40 window: https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/177821/ (shows heavy stalls in kv_recompute and router_select) :fire:
deploy-bot: Canary group created (5% traffic) with overrides from Mica. canary id: canary-177821-a. Starting at 04:00 UTC.
Lina G.: Also double-check RoPE scaling & head/kv dims in the Mixtral model config — earlier we had a mismatch between model metadata and runtime conv that can change attention scores subtly. not likely primary but should be ruled out.
Samir: I inspected model metadata; no RoPE scalar changes in the recent rollout. However, Mixtral uses smaller kv_dim per head in the MoE variant; numerical differences in kernel reorder may have stronger impact on low-dimension KV. worth testing a small rope_scale bump to see sensitivity.
Alex P.: Plan for the canary: (1) run overrides, (2) collect route_skew, kv_miss_rate, p95/p99 for 60m, (3) if kv_miss_rate > 8% or p95 doesn't improve, revert kernels and force f32 fallback. Who owns the revert? @Samir?
Samir: I'll own the revert path. quick rollback command saved: `redwood rollout revert canary-177821-a --force-kernel-fallback=f32_ref`
Mica Chen: Canary started. initial telemetry (first 10m): route_skew down 12%, kv_miss_rate to 6.2% (from 17%), p95 trending down ~8%. collecting further.
Lina G.: Nice. Also log the per-expert memory pressure and eviction timestamps — we want to see if evictions align with spikes in request concurrency.
perf-bot: 10m metrics snapshot: route_skew:-12%, kv_miss_rate:6.2%, p95:-8.1%, per_expert_queue_ms: -9%.
Alex P.: If this continues for 60m we should promote the kernel-selector change to add a guard for MoE models (prefer f32 path for Mixtral by default) until we can make int8 path numerically equivalent.
Samir: I'll open a follow-up perf ticket to trace exact reorder/pack differences and add a deterministic packing test to the kernel test-suite.
Mica Chen: 60m mark: metrics stable. I'll leave canary open for 2h and then trigger 25% if stable. posting logs and the router_logits dump to the incident channel as well.
Lina G.: Thanks team. Add note to runbook: "On kernel-selection changes, monitor MoE route entropy and KV cache miss rates within 30m" :white_check_mark:
Alex P.: Great job. moving this thread to postmortem once we have root cause details. :thumbsup:
